FR-001.title: The application MUST emit structured records for startup beginning, local player availability, application readiness, shutdown beginning, and successful shutdown completion.

FR-002.title: The application MUST emit an error record for a startup failure that the desktop host absorbs so the existing user-visible failure status can remain available.

FR-003.title: The player service MUST emit an error record when its background serving operation exits unexpectedly, while normal server closure MUST remain silent.

FR-004.title: The application MUST emit outcome records for session creation, session opening, demo copying, session saving, player-configuration loading, broadcast lifecycle commands, and public-access lifecycle or configuration commands.

FR-005.title: User-cancelled operations MUST be recorded as cancellations rather than failures, and expected validation rejections MUST not be escalated to fatal process errors.

FR-006.title: Event-delivery errors that are intentionally not returned to callers MUST be recorded with the affected event name.

FR-007.title: Records MUST use severity and structured fields to identify the operation, outcome, safe lifecycle state, revision, count, or error as applicable.

FR-008.title: Records MUST NOT contain provider tokens, player passwords, generated passwords, session content, terminal content, character names, or unredacted secret-store and provider error details.

FR-009.title: Logging MUST be initialized exactly once for the production application and MUST remain available throughout startup and shutdown.

FR-010.title: Logging MUST NOT change existing command results, runtime status, lifecycle ordering, resource cleanup, public/private capability boundaries, or persistence behavior.

FR-011.title: Automated tests MUST verify representative lifecycle, command-outcome, unexpected-serving, swallowed-event-error, and secret-redaction records.

context: area: root application lifecycle and desktop boundary
constraint: never log public-access secrets or user-authored gameplay content
constraint: github.com/obalunenko/logger is the required logging package
intent: Provide safe structured operational diagnostics across the application lifecycle and important Overseer actions.
expectations: No runtime log-file persistence, rotation, or logging settings UI.
Repository build tooling and browser-test fixture output are outside the logging migration.
approach: Initialize one structured logger at process startup, inject it into the root App and player server, and emit safe operational records only at lifecycle and trusted application boundaries. Use a shared test logger to verify fields, severity, swallowed errors, and redaction without mutating global state.

decisions.decision: Pin github.com/obalunenko/logger v1.2.0 as a production dependency
decisions.why: It is the user-selected latest stable package and exposes context and structured fields
decisions.rejected: standard-library log and alternative logging libraries

decisions.decision: Inject logger.Logger into App and player.Server
decisions.why: Deterministic parallel-safe tests without global logger mutation

decisions.decision: Log safe outcomes at operational boundaries
decisions.why: Preserves domain independence and avoids payload or credential disclosure
decisions.rejected: logging every domain method or complete request/result payloads
